description: We are 3 team members and we are complete.
summary: Stay Vertical created is an open web tool that searches Earth for terrain analogs of 18 lunar and Martian sites: 8 near the Moon's south pole (Artemis candidate regions) and 10 on Mars (rover landing sites and regions of interest). For each site it compares 3 km patches of terrain using eight relief features (slope, curvature, roughness) plus a shape correlation, at a common resolution. It offers two searches: a curated catalog of 50 Earth zones, and an automatic sweep in which the algorithm scans eleven whole bands of the planet (about 4.7 million patches) with no prior list of places. Each candidate gets an analog profile that separates fidelity (relief, temperature, aridity, air pressure) from logistics (climate suitability from NASA POWER), and states what Earth cannot reproduce. The tool also reports where the analogy breaks down: five steep sites, including Shackleton and Gale, have no close relief analog in the swept area. This helps teams choose where to test rovers, habitats and procedures, and shows which conditions no Earth site can stand in for.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Stay Vertical lets you pick a site on the Moon or Mars and see which places on Earth resemble it most in relief, with the climate and working conditions of each place. Code: https://github.com/kcarbzz/stayVertical

HOW IT WORKS

1. Common scale. Earth elevation is resampled to 80 m to compare with the Moon and to 200 m to compare with Mars. Every patch is about 3 km on a side.

2. Eight relief features per patch: mean, spread and 90th percentile of slope; mean and 90th percentile of curvature; median, 90th percentile and spread of roughness. Features are normalized with the median and interquartile range of the Earth patches.

3. Two stages. A physical stage keeps the Earth patches closest to the site in those eight features. A shape stage removes the overall tilt, smooths the relief and computes a Pearson correlation with the site, trying four rotations.

4. Two searches. A catalog of 50 Earth zones chosen by the team, and an automatic sweep of eleven bands (Puna and Altiplano, Iceland, Namib, central Australia, Canadian Arctic, Victoria Land and the Dry Valleys, central Sahara, Arabian Peninsula, Tibet and Qaidam, Gobi, Mojave and Great Basin): 745 one-degree tiles per body, 2.46 million patches for the Moon and 2.23 million for Mars. Forest, cropland, built-up areas, water, snow and ice are excluded with ESA WorldCover.

5. Analog profile. For every candidate, the site separates fidelity (relief shape, slope, temperature, aridity, air pressure against NASA reference values) from logistics (13 climate factors from NASA POWER, 2021-2025, with a provisional traffic light). It also lists what Earth cannot reproduce (gravity, vacuum or thin atmosphere, radiation) and what was not evaluated.

WHAT WE FOUND

- Jezero's best match is on Devon Island in the Canadian Arctic, about 70 km from Haughton crater, a classic Mars analog. The algorithm reached it with no prior list.

- Malapert and de Gerlache match terrain in Iceland; the steep lunar craters point to Antarctica.

- Five sites (Haworth, Shackleton, Faustini, Gale and Valles Marineris) have no close relief analog in the swept area: they are both very steep and smooth. We report this as a result, not a failure.

- Flat Martian plains have many near-identical Earth patches, so we present them as groups of equivalents, not a single twin.

BENEFITS AND INTENDED IMPACT

Mission teams, researchers and students can shortlist places to test rovers, habitats and field procedures, and can see at a glance which dimension of the analogy holds and which does not. A place that is colder and drier resembles Mars more but is harder to work in; the profile shows both.

TOOLS

Python (NumPy, SciPy, rasterio, pystac-client), JavaScript, HTML and CSS, Leaflet, GitHub Pages, Google Colab. The site runs fully in the browser with no server. A small neural network running in the browser (Vertikal Bot) explains the results shown. Available in Spanish and English.

WHAT IS CREATIVE

The search is systematic, not a list of famous sites; fidelity and logistics are scored separately; and the tool says where no analog exists.

LIMITS WE CONSIDERED

Only relief is compared: geology, ice, dust, illumination and the subsurface are not evaluated. The sweep covers eleven bands, not the whole Earth. Antarctica has no land-cover map, so a candidate there may lie on ice. Climate is a ~55 km grid cell, not the microclimate of a 3 km patch. Results are exploratory and do not certify any site.
